title: Is a live online class the right next step? A 2-minute parent quiz
summary: Not sure if your homeschooler needs a live class, tutor, or self-paced course? This 2-minute quiz matches your family's goals to the right format.
body_markdown:
### Mostly C's: 1-on-1 tutoring to close a specific gap


Your child needs targeted, patient instruction in one area. Group classes may move too fast or too slow. A tutor can diagnose the gap and build a plan around it.


Where to start:[Outschool's 1-on-1 tutoring](https://outschool.com/online-classes/tutoring) matches your child with a teacher who specializes in the subject and grade level where they need help. Sessions are flexible and scheduled on your timeline. If you're comparing options, our[tutoring comparison guide](https://outschool.com/articles/best-online-tutoring-kids-comparison) covers what to look for in a tutor and how platforms differ.


Using ESA funds? Tutoring is an approved expense in most state programs. Check what your state covers in our[ESA approved expenses guide](https://outschool.com/esa-guides/approved-list) .


### Mostly D's: enrichment classes for passionate learners


Your child doesn't need remediation. They need a teacher who geeks out about the same things they do, and a class that goes deeper than any textbook.


Where to start: Outschool's enrichment catalog is where this shines. Browse by interest:[coding and game design](https://outschool.com/online-classes/coding) ,[creative writing](https://outschool.com/online-classes/creative-writing) ,[science experiments](https://outschool.com/online-classes/science-experiments) ,[art](https://outschool.com/online-classes/art) ,[music](https://outschool.com/online-classes/music) , or niche interests like Minecraft architecture or veterinary science. Many of these classes become the highlight of a kid's week.


### A mix of answers? That's normal.


Most families don't fall neatly into one category. You might need tutoring for math and a social group class for everything else. Or your child might want enrichment but you also need it to count toward your learning plan. Live classes and tutoring are flexible: you can combine formats across subjects.


## How to evaluate whether a class is working


Give any new class or tutor at least 3 sessions before deciding. Here's what to watch for:


- **Engagement:** Is your child talking about the class between sessions? That's the strongest signal.
- **Teacher fit:** Does the teacher adjust to your child's pace and communication style?
- **Practical impact:** For academic subjects, is the skill gap closing? For enrichment, is your child building on what they learn?
- **Your week:** Does the class reduce your stress or add to it? The right class should make your homeschool week easier, not harder.


## What about cost?


Outschool classes range from about $10 to $25 per session for group classes, with 1-on-1 tutoring typically starting around $25 to $40 per session depending on the subject and teacher.


Families with education savings accounts can use ESA funds for Outschool classes in most participating states. If you're in Florida, Texas, Arizona, Alabama, or another ESA state, check our[ESA guide](https://outschool.com/esa-guides/what-is-education-savings-account) for how to connect your funds.


## Frequently asked questions


### Do I need to pick just one type of class?


No. Many families mix formats. A common pattern: 1-on-1 tutoring for the hardest subject, a weekly group class for social connection, and self-paced materials for everything else.


### What age range does Outschool cover?


Outschool classes are available for kids ages 3 to 18. Teachers design classes for specific age bands, so your child is always learning alongside peers at a similar level.


### Can I try a class before committing to a series?


Yes. Many Outschool classes are one-time sessions or flexible-schedule formats. You can try a single session before enrolling in a multi-week course.


### What if my child has a learning difference?


Outschool has a growing catalog of classes designed for neurodivergent learners, including ADHD-friendly formats, dyslexia-informed reading instruction, and sensory-aware teaching styles. Browse[classes for learning differences](https://outschool.com/online-classes/learning-differences) or filter by your child's specific need.
